hypothesis: Representing locally observable native CLI auth expiry as explicit readiness warning or stale states will let operators see risky harness-managed login state before unattended long-running autonomy depends on it, without adding provider network calls to default readiness.

metricsCompared.name: focused native CLI auth-expiry coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: readiness tests covered ready, missing, error, and unverifiable auth states but had no expiring or stale locally observable auth semantics
metricsCompared.candidate: 6 focused test files passed with 70 tests covering parser precedence, preset warning/failure aggregation, Gemini CLI cache states, doctor rendering, workflow capability artifacts, and harness-parity artifacts

metricsCompared.name: default readiness network posture
metricsCompared.baseline: native CLI readiness stayed local but could only report clean ready or coarse missing/unverifiable state
metricsCompared.candidate: local status-output parsing and documented Gemini CLI cache inspection surface expiry warnings and stale non-refreshable credentials without provider network calls

metricsCompared.name: repo validation
metricsCompared.baseline: task started from a ready item without expiring-auth readiness artifacts
metricsCompared.candidate: Biome, lint, typecheck, focused tests, and validate-tasks pass with the task moved to done and evidence stored in the run directory

rationale: The change is a narrow extension of existing harness readiness and preset aggregation surfaces. Expiring auth is intentionally pass-with-warning for non-refreshable near-expiry credentials, stale locally observable auth remains a failure, refreshable credentials stay ready, and unverifiable native auth remains unverifiable. Focused tests and redacted artifacts prove the behavior without introducing live provider calls.
